source: 'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' p3 (#p3) rail card block: `background:#fff;border:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.12);border-radius:10px;...;overflow:hidden` with a `height:3px;background:linear-gradient(90deg,#5A5552,#5A5552 22%,rgba(90,85,82,.18))` rule on the card's OWN top edge, then `padding:12px 16px 14px`; README.md §0.5 (AlphaSense place-keeping behaviour, "In this list · 4 of 15"); operator ruling 5.1
notes: Selector repair, train 58 (2026-09-07): the earlier `[data-section-rule]` selector never matched anything (no such attribute exists anywhere in the product). InThisListStat.tsx (like DetailSection and every other DetailShell.tsx card, confirmed by direct source read this session) DOES render the shared `SectionRule` component from `src/components/ui/SectionRule.tsx`, whose rendered marker is the class `.cl-section-rule`, not a data attribute — the selector below now measures the real element.
Padding differs: artboard `padding:12px 16px 14px` (top 12, bottom 14) vs the built card's `padding: 14px 16px` (top 14, bottom 14) — a small but real MISMATCH on padding-top.

The artboard's example reads "Action · 4 of 13 · sorted by next date" (a third clause, 'sorted by next date') where the built component renders "4 of 13 in Action" (order reversed, no sort clause) — this is a DATA/COPY difference, not a geometry one; logged as an observation, not asserted as a text MISMATCH since the exact numbers (4 of 13) are fixture-dependent on both sides.
